title: Adolescent perceptions of warning messages to counter online sexual abuse
abstract: Adolescent engagement online brings with it exposure to problematic and illegal online content and behaviours such as cyberbullying, image-based abuse, sexual extortion and child sexual abuse material. Online warning messages may help deter illegal and otherwise problematic online behaviour and direct victims to support services. However, the target audience must perceive these messages as useful. This mixed methods study sought feedback from adolescents (aged 16–18 years) on the perceived utility of online warning messages addressing various problematic online behaviours. Two hundred and ninety-eight participants completed the study, reading vignettes describing problematic online behaviours alongside image and text-based warning messages directed at victims, bystanders and/or offenders in these scenarios. Participants generally agreed that the warnings would attract the target’s attention and promote reflection or help-seeking. However, they believed victims were more likely than offenders to actively engage with support services. Participants were divided on preference for image-with-text or text-only warnings.
